links.comparator_used: Alerts generated but not sent to clinicians in control units, with standard RRT activation criteria used
links.outcome: Escalation rate per 1000 patient bed days (primary); cardiovascular medication orders; combined in-hospital and 30-day mortality
links.effect: Escalation 12.3 vs 11.3 per 1000 patient bed days (difference 1.0; 95% CI -2.8 to 4.7); IPTW adjusted IRR 1.43 (95% CI 1.16-1.78; p<0.001). Mortality 7% vs 9.3% (-2.4%; 95% CI -4.5% to -0.2%); IPTW adjusted RR 0.76 (95% CI 0.58-0.99; p=0.045).
links.tradeoff: Intervention patients were more likely to receive cardiovascular medication orders (16.1% vs 11.3%; IPTW adjusted RR 1.74; 95% CI 1.39-2.18). The IPTW adjusted escalation rate was higher with alerts.
links.quote: Real-time machine learning alerts do not reduce the rate of escalation but may reduce mortality.

design_hint: Routing ML deterioration alerts directly to front-line teams or rapid response team versus silent alerts
